comparator.name: Psychology (Psychologie)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current student curriculum establishes a 180-EC bachelor with 75 EC of compulsory major study, 60 EC of major choices and 45 EC of genuine profiling space. The compulsory major consists of eight first-year courses (60 EC) and a 15-EC bachelor research project. The coherent selected major-choice pathway uses the two first-listed thematic courses in their respective blocks, the first two listed research-skills trainings, compulsory Advanced Research Methods and Statistics, and three clinical-scientific theory courses. These choices total 60 EC. The generic target names no domain; the three domains are equally formal and may overlap, so the first-listed Clinical Scientific domain is selected by neutral official order. The 45-EC profiling space remains generic rather than being filled with invented subjects.

alternatives.label: Closest match to Psychology
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible psychology programme combining social, developmental, clinical, cognitive and organisational psychology with statistics, research methods, assessment-related study and cross-disciplinary perspectives on behaviour.
progression: The sociology sequence progresses from Introduction through Modern Sociology to Contemporary Social Theory; advanced psychology follows the psychology gateway and statistics.

alternatives.label: Brain & cognition
alternatives.concept: A Brain and Cognition route centred on cognitive neuroscience, perception, higher-order functions, language, biological foundations and quantitative/data-oriented research.
alternatives.distinctness: Neuroscience, life and health sciences, anatomy, physiology and data replace part of the broad psychology mix.
progression: Life-science foundations precede physiology, anatomy and laboratory work, then disease and pathology; cognition, psychology and data courses build from earlier gateways and methods, and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Psychology, leadership & organisations
alternatives.concept: A Work and Organisational Psychology route centred on organisational behaviour, leadership, diversity, negotiation, workplace wellbeing, behavioural decision-making and applied organisational research.
alternatives.labelReason: The broader label reflects the completed mix of psychology, leadership, organisations, sociology, communication, business and behavioural economics.
alternatives.distinctness: Organisational psychology and leadership replace the biological and cognitive emphasis.
progression: Psychology, business, sociology, methods and leadership foundations precede advanced organisational, communication and behavioural courses.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic broad Psychology bachelor. Utrecht groups later major choices into Clinical Scientific, Societal Scientific and Fundamental Scientific domains, allows overlap, and does not designate one as the general route. The first-listed Clinical Scientific domain is therefore selected as a neutral official-order tie-break, independently of UCR fit. Within the required thematic and research-skills choices, first-listed options are used in published order.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match covers Utrecht’s programme-wide psychology and research core. Brain and cognition and social and organisational psychology are independently evidenced, coherent, mechanically feasible and substantively distinct additional routes. Clinical/mental-health and developmental directions were also assessed, but three UCR alternatives is the maximum.

notes.text: Utrecht Psychology provides a structured disciplinary sequence with dedicated psychological methods, research-skills trainings, clinical theory and a supervised 15-EC bachelor project. UCR can build substantial psychology, cognition and organisational programmes, but it does not reproduce the same specialist practical sequence or professional clinical preparation.
